items.title: 한국어 책 166톤 미국 반출… AI 학습 시대, 출판 저작권의 숙제
items.excerpt: 선적 기록상 165.69톤(약 41만 권)의 한국어 책이 웅진북센→Better World Books를 거쳐 Anthropic 도서 조달 유통망으로 반출돼 스캔 후 폐기된 것으로 전해졌다.
items.rationale: New concrete revelation: shipping records trace about 410,000 Korean-language books through Woongjin Booxen to Anthropic's scanning supply chain. Chosen over the Yomiuri Japan story (one-at-most rule) and the 주간동아 bulk-buying piece, which covers the same theme.

items.title: Author denies allegations she used AI to write book after novel 'dropped by agent'
items.excerpt: Author Kathryn O'Connor Mertens has issued a statement denying allegations that she used AI to write her novel Wild Horse Country, saying she has drafts, handwritten notes and research to demonstrate she wrote the book herself.
items.rationale: A fresh AI-authorship accusation that cost an author her agent. It shows writers why keeping a paper trail of drafts and notes matters now.

items.title: Les éditeurs belges veulent un label « sans IA » pour rassurer les lecteurs
items.excerpt: Belgian publishers are considering a 'without AI' certification label and a price adjustment for books published in Belgium to protect quality and frame AI use.
items.rationale: A national publishers' push for a 'sans IA' certification label plus a pricing measure. This is an industry-level initiative, separate from the private Proudly Human scheme carded on 11-07.

items.title: Anthropic has started paying out its copyright settlement to authors
items.excerpt: Novelist Courtney Milan says she has already received her share of Anthropic's $1.5B settlement; the full payout should be about $3,000 per book, with part still to come early next year.
items.rationale: Follow-up on the Bartz settlement with a new concrete event: authors are now receiving payments (about $3,000 per book, the rest due early next year).

items.title: IFWG and IPI Comics put their ban on AI-made work into contracts
items.excerpt: IFWG Publishing and IPI Comics wrote an AI-made-work ban into contracts and pledged to keep books out of training deals; Candlemark & Gleam makes authors certify how they wrote.
items.rationale: Independent presses are writing AI bans and training opt-outs into their author contracts. That is a concrete contract change authors will see when they sign.

https://www.theverge.com/ai-artificial-i.new_action: Anthropic's $1.5B settlement has begun paying authors directly (about $3,000 per book, remainder due early 2027). This comes after the 11-18 claim-deadline card and the 11-21 WotC-sharing card.
